image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a male mallard duck (drake) floating on water. The duck is facing left but looking back over its shoulder towards the right. It features a glossy iridescent green head, a distinct white neck ring, a yellow-green bill, and a mottled brown and grey body. The tail shows characteristic curled black feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and exhibits the correct yellow-green coloration with a dark tip.
The visible eye is small, round, and distinctly black/dark brown, matching the biological description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body appears robust and floats naturally on the water surface. The feather texture looks dense and layered, consistent with waterproof plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic Mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, clear white neck ring, and mottled brown/grey body feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck is floating on water, and the legs/feet are submerged and completely occluded from view. Cannot verify anatomy.
The folded wing structure is visible along the side of the body, appearing compact and aerodynamic as expected for a swimming bird.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear, showing the characteristic upward curl of the central black feathers (drake feathers) and white undertail coverts.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Mallard Drake) and rule out hybrid or nonsensical bird features.
To detect subtle texture anomalies in the feathers or unnatural blending at the waterline, which are common AI artifacts.
To ensure the body is a single continuous manifold without floating feathers or structural disconnections.
To verify the physical interaction between the duck and the water (displacement/reflection) is geometrically consistent.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the green head and the white neck ring; AI often blurs this boundary. Verify that the 'curl' of the tail feathers has actual 3D volume and isn't just a painted-on texture. Check for any 'melting' of the bill into the face.
